pr_body:
Adding implementations that will check shards status and report health
status based on their availability

Closes: #83240
Related to: #83303
pr_comments: Hi @idegtiarenko, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

Here is what I have for what is being produced in this indicator:

```
"shards": {
  "status": "yellow",
  "summary": "This cluster has 13 shards including 7 primaries ([.geoip_databases][0] unreplicated) and 6 replicas ([my_first_index3][1] unallocated), ([my_first_index3][0] unallocated), ([my_first_index][1] unallocated), ([my_first_index][0] unallocated), ([my_first_index2][1] unallocated), ([my_first_index2][0] unallocated).",
  "details": {
    "allocated_primaries_count": 7,
    "allocated_replicas_count": 0,
    "unreplicated_primaries_count": 1,
    "unreplicated_primaries": [
      "[.geoip_databases][0]"
    ],
    "initializing_primaries_count": 0,
    "initializing_primaries": [],
    "unallocated_replicas_count": 6,
    "unallocated_replicas": [
      "[my_first_index3][1]",
      "[my_first_index3][0]",
      "[my_first_index][1]",
      "[my_first_index][0]",
      "[my_first_index2][1]",
      "[my_first_index2][0]"
    ],
    "restarting_replicas_count": 0,
    "restarting_replicas": [],
    "unallocated_primaries_count": 0,
    "unallocated_primaries": []
  }
}
```

I think that we need a few adjustments. First, I'm not sure `shards` is the correct name. As I have mentioned there are other health indicators that we may want to eventually add. For example a relocating shard that is stuck. At the same time we could conceivably add that under a generalized `shards` health indicator. I just wonder if we should go with `shard_assignment`. I'm not sure `shard_allocation` makes sense as that also would include a stuck shard. The name here probably should get wider input. `shard_availability`?

Second, on this first PR I think we want to pare down the information. Including names of shards is unnecessary at the moment as I think that is an entire discussion. The current approach produces unbounded responses. 

Third, I think we probably want to go with `assigned/unassigned`. Or `available/unavailable`. Those seem like the most consistent terms currently. 

Fourth, I do not think we want unreplicated primaries to currently be reported or impact health status. This default cluster has a built-in unreplicated index (.geoip_databases). It would always be yellow no matter what the user does! Unreplicated seems like cluster advice at the moment, not a health status.

Fifth, at the moment I think we only need to report "bad" or "pertinent" stuff in the details. As in unassigned or restarting. No need to included the number of assigned.

Sixth, I think we want an initializing_replicas status for `replicaShard.initializing()`. I think initializing replica shards should leave the cluster green. Although this is different behavior from cluster health currently. So we should confirm on this point.

```
"assigned_shards": {
  "status": "yellow",
  "summary": "This cluster has 6 unassigned replicas.",
  "details": {
    "unassigned_primaries_count": 0,
    "unassigned_replicas_count": 6,
    "initializing_primaries_count": 0,
    "initializing_replicas_count": 0,
    "restarting_replicas_count": 0
  }
}
```

I think we should pare down the summaries too. It is possible that it could be used to drive a banner interface.

"summary": "This cluster has 6 unassigned replicas."
"summary": "This cluster has 5 unassigned primaries."
"summary": "This cluster has 2 unassigned primaries and 4 unassigned replicas."
"summary": "This cluster has no unassigned shards."

Also, we need more discussion I think around this concept of a shard that is unassigned, but not like concerning. "restarting" is a good example. From an elasticsearch perspective, "restarting" is unassigned. I don't really love the idea of us filtering out special cases with different names. I definitely think the special cases make sense to pick appropriate health statuses. I feel like a "restarting_replica" shard is unassigned it should still be counted as unassigned. Just not contribute to a yellow status.

```
"assigned_shards": {
  "status": "green",
  "summary": "This cluster has 3 unassigned replicas.",
  "details": {
    "unassigned_primaries_count": 0,
    "unassigned_replicas_count": 3,
    "initializing_primaries_count": 0,
    "initializing_replicas_count": 0,
    "restarting_replicas_count": 3
  }
}
```

This raises the question about summary there as there is no indication that this is a case where the unassignment is fine. I don't know if it is possible to work the word "expected" in there?

"summary": "This cluster has 6 unassigned replicas for unexpected reasons."
"summary": "This cluster has 5 unassigned primaries for unexpected reasons."
"summary": "This cluster has 2 unassigned primaries and 4 unassigned replicas for unexpected reasons."
"summary": "This cluster has no unassigned shards for unexpected reasons."

A lof of "un"s going on there though.

Or "expected"

"summary": "This cluster has 6 expected replicas unassigned."
"summary": "This cluster has 5 expected primaries unassigned."
"summary": "This cluster has 2 expected primaries and 4 expected unassigned."
"summary": "All expected shards are assigned."

or "unavailable" but "unavailable" has a meaning of shards that are unhealthy for unknown/bad reasons

"summary": "This cluster has 6 replicas unavailable."
"summary": "This cluster has 5 primaries unavailable."
"summary": "This cluster has 2 primaries and 4 replicas unavailable."
"summary": "All shards are available."


Finally, we need more discussion about unavailable vs. unassigned. Cloud is currently using "unavailable" and that might be a better high level term for users.

On a separate note, we have an ask to add impact level statements to the indicators as these will be valuable to the Cloud banner. And we are not ready to work on coalescing different impacts at the moment. Something like:

"This cluster has 4 indices with ingest and search functionality disrupted and 3 indices with search scalability and redundancy disrupted."

But we can probably leave that out of this first PR. Probably need a broader discussion of summary vs. impact.

I largely share Tim's views above.

It's unclear to me whether our goal here is to replicate the existing behaviour or to extend it to something that's more focussed on how users should react to a non-green health report. We're definitely going beyond the existing behaviour but we're not really doing anything to help users turn the more detailed information we're giving them into concrete actions. I think it would be ok not to go beyond the existing behaviour in the first iteration, but if we are wanting to get closer to the end goal then we should think more about those actions.

I think we cannot simply ignore missing shard copies due to restarting nodes as some action may be needed even in this case. For instance, it seems safe enough to ignore missing copies for read-only shards (at least as long as the remaining copies can cope with the search load) but if there's a write to a shard while one or more copies are missing then that write is not properly replicated which puts it at risk. The user could pause indexing to avoid this kind of problem, so that seems like something to raise with yellow status. Also if the restarting node doesn't come back within some reasonable timeout then do we stop considering it expected and start raising more warnings about the missing node?

What about having a list of possible `user impact`s? And this list can be mapped to the list of all possible `summary`s?

For example, `user impact` could be:
- "Some of your ingest and search functionality may be disrupted" <-> when only primaries unassigned.
- "Some of your ingest and search functionality may be disrupted" <-> when both primaries and replicas are unassigned.
- "Some of your search scalability and redundancy may be disrupted." <-> when only replicas are unassigned.

And users can further click on the banner to learn a detailed summary: 
- "summary": "This cluster has 6 replicas unavailable."
- "summary": "This cluster has 5 primaries unavailable."
- "summary": "This cluster has 2 primaries and 4 replicas unavailable."
- "summary": "All shards are available."

----
The user impact wording from kibana currently have the following when shards failed:
```
The data you are seeing might be incomplete or wrong.
```
Is it worth being synced with Kibana?

> Also if the restarting node doesn't come back within some reasonable timeout then do we stop considering it expected and start raising more warnings about the missing node?

I'd like to consider the health status green until the shutdown for restarts allocation delay has timed out (as long as there is a primary ofc). This is how our solution is designed wrt. rolling restarts and I prefer not to flag health issues when no action is needed by users. If a client application needs a flag for whether to pause any indexing, we should provide that through an explicit API instead.

issue_context.title: Implement health indicator for shard allocation
issue_context.body:
### Description

Implement health indicator for shard allocation.
This indicator should have same or similar behavior to existing health endpoint.

Aspects to be considered:
* nodes scheduled for reboot should not cause cluster to go yellow (but could cause it go red)
* huge number of unallocated shards should not cause response bloat.
* consider showing allocation explain if possible

Rel: TBD

review_comments: I suppose we do not trigger on this, but neither do we on recovery. I wonder if we should randomize between more causes here, like `NODE_LEFT`, `PRIMARY_FAILED` and more?
May be. Due to the way how shards are constructed this could be done by adding more `ShardState` and extending this method with additional simulation
I think this should include `RELOCATING` too? So that relocating shards also count as started?
According to the line above it is always not null
nit: did you consider implement a `getSummary()` method in ShardAllocationCounts directly, and call the methods here?
Yes, but I did not come up with a good way to merge distinct messages. It would require appending primary/primaries/replica/replicas suffixes as well as properly setting comas.
I think we should add this for replicas too (checking for yellow status when restart has expired).

I think we need to special handle new indices similar to [`ClusterShardHealth`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/12ad399c488f0cc60e19b5e1b29c6d569cb4351a/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/health/ClusterShardHealth.java#L201). I think we should report green for now for shards of such new indices in this PR, since there will need to be some interaction with allocation to see if this is unassigned due to throttling or because the shard cannot be assigned at all currently.

A separate count of the "new" unassigned/initializing shards seems necessary.

Can we construct this with the shutdown metadata instead, such that we only pass the node shutdowns in the constructor? Would look cleaner to me. Also, can we pass just a `Function<String, SingleNodeShutdownMetadata` like:
```suggestion
        var status = new ShardAllocationStatus(shutdown.getAllNodeMetadataMap()::get);
```
Nodes shutdown is not required for output and only used for calculation. I believe it is better to keep such dependencies as arguments

I do not agree, by having the `addPrimary/Replica` methods accept the shutdowns input as well, a specific implementation is dictated, where the information is resolved immediately rather than on output. But given the localness of the code, I can live with how it is for now.

I would still like to see us just pass around `Function<String, SingleNodeShutdownMetadata>` rather than the full metadata.

> I would still like to see us just pass around Function<String, SingleNodeShutdownMetadata> rather than the full metadata.

I agree with Henning on this
Currently this is indicator is not turning yellow/red once `allocation_delay` is reached. I am working on fixing that

We should ideally also trigger on initializing shards. This may have some complication to integrate with restart though if the operator/orchestration waits for green or yellow `_cluster/health` before removing the restart indication it might work out ok.

I think deferring to a follow-up is fine, but perhaps add a comment here to aid the next reader?
